languages.title: Languages — Lingogram
languages.description: Lingogram's site in 42 languages — pick the one you read in.
languages.lede: The whole site is translated into {n} languages. Pick yours — every page you're reading now has a version in it.
languages.noMatchHint: Try its English name, or its two-letter code.

footer.tagline: Learn languages from what you watch.

demo.hintPrefix: This demo is the real extension, running on this page —
demo.hintSuffix: to save it, or try a mode below.

dual.p: The line you hear next to the line you understand — no pausing, no switching tracks.

guess.h: Click to reveal — and train your ear
guess.p: The line stays hidden until you click it. Guess from listening first, then check yourself: the gap between the two is exactly where hearing improves.

single.h: On screen, or in the sidebar — your call
single.p: Keep both lines over the film, where your eyes already are. Or take them off with one button and read from the panel instead, at your own pace. The subtitles never disappear — they just move.

save.p: Select a word — one tap saves it with the sentence it came from, straight to your dictionary right here on lingogram.ai.

editionsCard.yt: Fills the missing second track with YouTube's auto-translation.
editionsCard.nf: Original subtitle tracks, no machine translation.
editionsCard.hd: Dual tracks when a title carries them.

home.heroLede: Watch with subtitles in two languages, or train your ear by revealing only the words you didn't catch. Save new words to your personal dictionary.
home.ctaSecondary: Pick the edition for the site you watch on ↓
home.platformsH2: One Lingogram, tuned for the site you watch on
home.platformsLede: Each edition is a separate Chrome extension, built for one site's player — native subtitle tracks, fullscreen overlay, the fixes that site needs. They share the same learning tools and the same account, so your saved words are in one place whichever you use. Two extensions cover all three sites: the YouTube one handles Netflix as well.
home.editionSoonBody: New dedicated editions ship regularly — tell us where you watch.
home.howH2: From install to first saved word in one video
home.step1D: Choose the language you're learning and your own. A quick one-time setup — no account needed.
home.step2D: Press play — both languages appear together, on the video and in a transcript that scrolls with the scene.
home.step3T: Save words, review them on this site
home.step3D: Keep a word in one tap while you watch — then open your dictionary on this site and review it with the scene it came from.
home.dictH2: Every word you save builds a dictionary that's actually yours
home.dictLede: Not a frequency list from a textbook — words you met in scenes you chose, kept with the lines they came from. Whatever edition you watch with, everything lands in one account, and it's waiting for you on this site after you log in.
home.dictCtx1: “He {w} agreed to drive the getaway car.”
home.dictCtx3: “We've been {w} since the last gas station.”
home.dictFoot: Your words sync across devices and every Lingogram edition — {b}.
home.featH2: Most tools stop at translation. Lingogram makes words stick.
home.featLede: Lingogram is based on active recall: you don't just read along — you guess, replay, and collect, so the hours you already spend watching turn into real progress.
home.feat1P: Catch every line in the original and match it to your own language without pausing. When you're ready, hide the translation — dual subtitles are a starting point, and Lingogram helps you outgrow them.
home.feat2H: Replay the line, not the movie
home.feat2P: The transcript scrolls with the video on its own. Click any line to jump back and loop that one scene until the sounds you couldn't parse become words you instantly recognize.
home.feat3P: Words start hidden: catch the line by ear, then reveal it. This listen-first loop builds listening you can rely on — not subtitles you only read along to. Toggle it with {kbd}.
home.feat4P: One tap saves a word with the subtitle lines around it. It goes straight to {link} on lingogram.ai, where you review every word in its original scene.
home.privH2: What you watch stays your business
home.priv1: {b} Language and layout settings are stored locally in your browser.
home.priv2: {b} Subtitles are processed right on your device.
home.priv2Bold: We never see your watch history.
home.priv3: {b} If you sign in, we store your email and your saved words — nothing else, and we never sell them.
home.priv4: {b} If a site update breaks something, one click reports it so we can fix it fast.
home.finalH2: Turn tonight's episode into your language lesson
home.finalProof: Free · Sets up in under a minute

free.a: Yes. Dual subtitles, the transcript, and Guess mode are free. A free account is only needed if you want your saved words synced across devices.

languages.a: Any pair the video has captions for. On YouTube, if one of your two languages is missing, Lingogram fills it with YouTube's automatic translation so you still get the dual view. On Netflix and HDrezka it shows the subtitle tracks the title actually has — no machine translation.

edition.a: The one for the site you watch on. There are two extensions: one covers YouTube and Netflix together, the other covers HDrezka. Install both if you watch on both — they share the same learning tools and the same account, so your saved words stay in one place.

words.q: Where are my saved words kept?
words.a: In your personal dictionary, right here on lingogram.ai. Log in and every word you've saved is there with the scene it came from — whichever edition or device you saved it on.
